**hypothesis**: Does making the robot practice standing up from lying completely flat much more often teach it to tuck its splayed front legs under the body instead of pressing up on them until the motors overload? Flat-start rise is now the SOLE structural failure of the mesh-native-ref recipe: it fails identically (front legs never tuck, radial press-up pinned at 2.64A, h_err_end 24-28mm) at 2M in both canary seeds AND in both full-8M seed-0 replicates (acq8m + the dup-killed meshref-8m, which finished 8.06M before its kill and scored exactly canary level — proving the 2M->8M budget delta is within same-seed run-to-run noise). Yet flat starts get only ~17.5% of training exposure (rise_rsi_frac 0.5 x rise_flat_frac 0.35). Single lever, config-only, the mechanism the rung-9 grid pre-registered: within the non-rsi half, reweight flat/partial/crouch 0.35/0.40/0.25 -> 0.70/0.20/0.10, doubling flat exposure to ~35%; rsi/crouch curricula and everything else identical to the meshref 2M canary (this arm is funded by acq8m's PARTIAL clause: one targeted arm at the named residual subclass, never more undirected budget). Prediction-if-true: flat episodes learn the tuck while std is still high, converting the last over_current class. Prediction-if-false: flat stays a 2.64A press-up even at double exposure - exposure is not the lever, the tuck needs ref-content/phase treatment (tuck-phase anchor dose or tuck-segment curriculum), pre-register that next.

**verdict**: CANARY FAIL - MECHANISM: doubling flat-start exposure did NOT teach the tuck - and the dig-in found why no exposure dose ever could: the BC anchor itself skips the tuck. Flat-pinned probe (primary evidence, det+sto n=6+6, DR-0, pod): 0/12 valid_plant, every episode the identical 2.64A never-tucks press-up (zero swings, h_err_end 24-70mm) - the gate's pre-registered FAIL branch fires exactly. Standard DR-0 gate: flat 0/6 (same signature), non-flat sto 4/4 clean (h_err 0.1-7.8mm, cur_p95 0.63-2.19A) but non-flat det 0/2 (both rsi pinned 2.64A) - the flat-heavy mix if anything HURT non-flat det starts. ROOT CAUSE (code+ref audit, sim_env.py:4097-4111 + rise_ref_mesh_scripted.npz): the state-aligned anchor's height-floor lookahead (train.bc_anchor_min_h_ahead_mm=8) requires the target ref tick to be >=8mm above CURRENT chassis height, but the scripted ref's entire tuck phase (ticks 0-245, 4.9s) is height-FLAT (-0.1..+1.6mm, belly carries the mass by design). From ANY tuck-phase state the floored target lands at tick 257+ = the PRESS phase - the anchor (coef 3.0) supervises press-up-NOW from the sprawled pose on every flat start, skipping all 245 tuck ticks. Exposure dosing multiplies the WRONG supervision; explains the deterministic 2.64A signature and why pace/budget/dose all failed. The tuck sweeps ~90deg mean joint angle, so nearest-q pursuit advances without the floor; floor=0 (the code default; never run on the mesh ref - only 15/8/4/2 ever used) restores tuck supervision config-only. Next: tuckfloor0 canary pair (min_h_ahead_mm=0, everything else = meshref recipe) - this IS the FAIL branch tuck-phase treatment, sharpened from dose to defect-removal.
